subject: Billing preflight & commercial path — BrightForge (post-call)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@brightforge.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call summary & billing preflight — BrightForge

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we walked through so your procurement and finance teams can take next steps.

Summary of options we covered:
- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest onboarding, per-token billing, supports card and invoice (PO) with net terms. No infra commitment.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): predictable throughput, lower unit cost with commits (monthly/annual). Billing typically via PO with committed spend.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): for regulated workloads; procurement + legal engagement expected, usually enterprise contract + PO.

Key procurement questions from your side I noted:
1) Billing route: PO (net terms) vs card? You said procurement prefers PO and net45 but wanted confirmation from finance.
2) Marketplace interest: you asked if AWS Marketplace listing is acceptable to skip some procurement paperwork.
3) Commitment preference: whether you want dedicated reserved commits (discounts) or start on-hosted on-demand while procurement runs.

Next actions I committed to:
- Share a concise pricing summary and SOW template (attached).
- Draft a formal quote that includes both: (A) hosted, card + invoice options and (B) dedicated reserved commit option (12-month and 36-month) for procurement review.
- Flag marketplace onboarding steps and approximate timeline.

Can you confirm: 1) primary finance contact (name & email) and 2) whether BrightForge requires PO number on first invoice or on all invoices?

If procurement wants a one-pager checklist to hand to finance (PO vs card, DocuSign vs Marketplace), I can send that today.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Hi Stephanie —

Great recap — thank you. Quick answers from procurement: we prefer PO billing with net45 on initial contracts. Our purchasing team (procure@brightforge.com) will want the SOW and a formal PDF quote that includes the exact billing cadence and whether Redwood can accept PO via AWS Marketplace (preferred) or if we need to process a standard Redwood invoice.

Notes / asks from my side:
- Marketplace is usually shorter for internal approvals, but legal will still want to review the terms. Is Redwood listed on AWS Marketplace for the dedicated commit SKU or just hosted API?
- If we go dedicated with commits, do you have a minimum monthly commit for a discount tier? Our ops team is also evaluating whether private deployment is necessary for some regulated models.
- I attached our procurement worksheet to show the approvals queue and internal PO flow.

Procurement contact: Nora Patel <nora.patel@brightforge.com> (she manages PO intake).

Can you produce the formal quote and indicate an estimated lead time for marketplace enablement if we choose that route?

Best,
Aisha

Hi Aisha / Stephanie —

Quick technical/commercial notes to include in the formal quote (so procurement has context):

1) Hosted (Redwood API)
- No minimum commit; billing is per-token. Can accept card immediately. Invoice/PO accepted with net terms once sales ops completes credit application (typical 5–7 business days).

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Discount tiers: 10% @ 12-month commit (>= $25k/month committed), 18% @ 24-month, 25% @ 36-month. Minimum monthly commit for dedicated is $25k USD (we can show an example commit table in the quote).
- Billing is usually PO/invoice for committed contracts. Marketplace options: we support AWS Marketplace but reserved commit SKUs require an additional listing process (see marketplace note below).

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Typically requires an enterprise agreement and a statement of work. Onboarding 4–8 weeks depending on infra and legal.

Marketplace enablement (high level):
- If BrightForge wants to buy via AWS Marketplace, we can provide a listing for hosted API within ~2–3 weeks (if no custom pricing). For dedicated commit SKUs, marketplace listing + billing path typically takes 3–4 weeks and requires coordination with our partnerships team.

I will draft the commit vs on-demand SKU table and attach to the quote. Stephanie — I suggest including both options (on-demand hosted + dedicated 12/36 month commit) so procurement can choose.

Thanks,
Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

I've prepared the formal quote (attached) that includes: hosted on-demand pricing (card + invoice options), dedicated commit examples (12/36-month tiers with the discount table Marcus referenced), and a short notes section on marketplace enrollment steps.

Traceable items for procurement:

- Marketplace: we support AWS Marketplace for hosted now; dedicated commit listing will need an extra 2–3 weeks of setup with partnerships.
- Lead times: invoice-based onboarding (credit application): 5–7 business days. Marketplace enablement: 2–4 weeks. Private deployment: estimate 4–8 weeks after contract sign.
